svg.text: The Context Sovereign Thesis: Unmanaged Transcripts vs. Active Working-Set Pruning
Why unbounded transcript accumulation exhausts model context windows, and how Elpis maintains a lean working set with durable evidence.

g.text: 1. Unmanaged Transcript Bloat (Codex)
80%–90% of prompt tokens are dead-end searches and historical tool outputs.
Turn 1: Exhaustive Ripgrep / AST Search
Tool Output: 231 lines of search results (4,800 tokens)
✗ Carried in full across every subsequent prompt
Turn 2: Bulky Cargo Test & Build Logs
Tool Output: 500 lines of compilation & passing tests (6,200 tokens)
✗ Clutters attention; model pays to re-read passed test suites
Turn 3: Multi-File Git Diff
Tool Output: 12 modified files (4,100 tokens)
✗ Agent only edits 1 function; 11 unreferenced diffs pollute window
Outcome: Escalating Context Pressure (>90% Bloat)
• Context explodes to 216k tokens; attention degrades significantly
• Triggers 3 emergency native compactions that destroy working state
• High per-request dollar cost on prompt tokens
2. Sovereign Evidence Governance (Elpis)
Selective Ace pruning at 30% threshold; raw logs saved to disk.
Turn 1: Pruned Finding + Evidence Pointer
Ace Distillation: [Found theme_picker at line 283] (65 tokens)
✓ 98.7% token reduction; raw output preserved in rollout:// evidence
Turn 2: Distilled Failure Assertion
Ace Distillation: [AssertionError at test_auth.rs:82] (110 tokens)
✓ 98.2% token reduction; 100% ground-truth error evidence retained
Turn 3: Distilled Targeted Edit
Ace Distillation: [Diff summary for auth_token.rs] (95 tokens)
✓ 97.6% token reduction; unreferenced file noise evicted
Outcome: Bounded in 20%–30% Safe Green Band
• Stabilized at 26.6%–27.1% median context across all 3 runs
• 0 native compactions; exact evidence recoverable on disk
• Preserves active model attention and predictable inference cost
